walkthroughs.body_html:
Biological Resources — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biological Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biological Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued food can't keep up with population (1798)?
options: Darwin
Malthus
Marx
Smith

mcqs.q: Shift from high to low birth/death rates is called?
options: Demographic transition
Carrying capacity
Population pyramid
Mortality crisis

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: Industrial chemicals being dumped.
It is a play about poor people.
Shared resources tend to be overexploited because individuals benefit personally while sharing costs.
Common land in medieval Britain.

mcqs.q: Why is a cold winter not evidence against climate change?
options: Cold winters are caused by warming.
It is evidence - if it gets cold sometimes, warming must be wrong.
Common land in medieval Britain.
Climate refers to long-term averages, not individual weather events.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Common land in medieval Britain.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Malthusian theory”?
options: Area of productive land needed to sustain a person's consumption and absorb their waste.
Faster use of non-renewables (minerals, fossil fuels) than they form or can be substituted.
Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resource depletion”?
options: Faster use of non-renewables (minerals, fossil fuels) than they form or can be substituted.
Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.
